name: Slack
verdict_reason: Per-seat pricing means the math flips hard around 4 seats — a 10-person team escapes $1,050/yr for one weekend of setup. Worth it if someone genuinely owns the pager; chat is the one service your team notices being down within 90 seconds.
what_you_lose: Slack's mobile push reliability — Mattermost push routes through their relay or you build your own, and half-working push kills adoption
The integration directory: webhooks exist, but every SaaS ships a Slack app and maybe a Mattermost one
Message history import is one-way and lossy — the escape is easier before the archive matters

what_broke: The image ships no shell, curl or wget, so a CMD-SHELL healthcheck fails forever while the server is fine — exec-form mmctl system status --local (with local mode enabled) is the probe that works
First admin account creation is a UI step — plan it into the rollout, whoever clicks first owns the workspace

notes: The economics inputs above are for ONE seat, which is the honest per-person floor — multiply the price by your seat count and the self-host cost barely moves. That asymmetry is the whole argument.
